script-retroflex-stops.title: Extra Letters: ټ ډ ڼ
script-retroflex-stops.pattern: ت → ټ    د → ډ    ن → ڼ
script-retroflex-stops.explanation: These three Pashto letters are the familiar Farsi/Dari letters ت (t), د (d), and ن (n) with a small ring added. The ring means: curl the tip of your tongue back and up to touch the roof of your mouth, then release. That gives a "harder," retroflex version of the sound -- something like the American English t/d/n in "bird" or "party."
script-retroflex-stops.fact: These retroflex rings are one of the fastest ways to spot Pashto at a glance -- if you see a small loop worked into a ت, د, or ن, you're reading Pashto, not Persian.

script-retroflex-fricatives.title: Extra Letters: ړ ږ ښ
script-retroflex-fricatives.pattern: ر → ړ    ز/ژ → ږ    س/ش → ښ
script-retroflex-fricatives.explanation: This trio is usually the hardest part of Pashto pronunciation for a Farsi speaker, because none of the three sounds exist in Farsi/Dari at all. ړ is a retroflex r -- curl the tongue back like for ټ, but let air flow around it. ږ and ښ are retroflex versions of z/zh and s/sh: same tongue curl, with a hiss of air passing by it.
script-retroflex-fricatives.fact: Pronunciation of ښ and ږ varies a lot by region -- some speakers say ښ closer to "kh," others closer to "sh." That's one reason Pashto dialects can sound quite different from each other even to native speakers.

script-affricates.title: Extra Letters: ځ څ
script-affricates.pattern: (no Farsi letter) → ځ (dz)    (no Farsi letter) → څ (ts)
script-affricates.explanation: ځ and څ aren't modified Farsi letters at all -- they're genuinely new letters for sounds Farsi doesn't have. ځ sounds like the "dz" in English "adze," and څ sounds like the "ts" in English "cats." Say those English sounds and you're most of the way to pronouncing them correctly.
script-affricates.fact: څلور (four) is one of the very first number words most learners meet, and it already uses څ -- so if you've done the numbers lesson, you've been reading څ without realizing it.

script-g-and-vowels.title: Extra Letters: ګ ې ۍ
script-g-and-vowels.pattern: گ → ګ (same sound)    (no letter in Farsi) → ې    ی → ۍ
script-g-and-vowels.explanation: ګ makes exactly the same "g" sound as Farsi's گ -- it's purely a different way of drawing the letter (a ring instead of two strokes on top), standard in Afghan Pashto printing. ې is a vowel letter Farsi doesn't write out -- it spells a short "e" sound. ۍ is a special ending: ی (the letter Farsi and Pashto share for "y") with a small hook added, marking many feminine nouns.
script-g-and-vowels.fact: ۍ is why so many Pashto words for "a female X" or "a small X" end the same way -- کورنۍ (family), نجلۍ (girl), and ماڼۍ (building) all carry it.
